outline.description: This chapter introduces the core problem: while large-scale unsupervised language models possess vast knowledge, they lack precise control and alignment with human values. It sets the stage for why 'alignment' is necessary for safe and useful AI.
subtopics: Capabilities and limitations of unsupervised pre-training
The challenge of steerability: selecting desired behaviors from internal knowledge
Overview of the alignment pipeline: from pre-training to instruction-tuning
Introduction to the Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback (RLHF) paradigm
The core motivation for Direct Preference Optimization (DPO)

outline.chapter_title: Foundations of RLHF and Preference Modeling
outline.description: Before understanding DPO, students must understand the traditional RLHF pipeline. This chapter covers the mathematical foundations of how humans express preferences and how rewards are traditionally modeled.
subtopics: Supervised Fine-Tuning (SFT): The first step in alignment
Human preference data collection: Pairwise comparisons
The Bradley-Terry (BT) Model: Modeling human choice mathematically
Reward Model Training: Parameterizing and optimizing $r(x, y)$
The RLHF objective: Maximizing reward with KL-divergence constraints

outline.chapter_title: The Bottlenecks of Reinforcement Learning in Alignment
outline.description: This chapter analyzes why the standard RLHF approach (using PPO) is difficult to implement in practice, providing the justification for the DPO method.
subtopics: Complexity of the RLHF pipeline (multiple models, sampling loops)
Instability of Actor-Critic algorithms like PPO
The 'Value Function' problem and the need for reward normalization
Computational costs of sampling from the LM policy during training
Hyperparameter sensitivity in traditional RLHF

outline.description: The core technical chapter of the textbook. It walks the student through the mathematical derivation that allows us to bypass RL and use a simple classification loss.
subtopics: The optimal policy of the KL-constrained reward maximization problem
The change-of-variables: mapping rewards to policy probabilities
Canceling the partition function in the Bradley-Terry model
Defining the DPO loss function: A binary cross-entropy objective
Mechanistic understanding: Analyzing the DPO gradient
Weighting mechanism: Preventing model degeneration during updates

outline.description: This chapter provides the academic rigor behind the paper, explaining why DPO is theoretically sound and how it relates to existing RLHF frameworks.
subtopics: Equivalence relations of reward functions
The representability theorem: DPO and the class of reward models
Comparison of DPO's implicit reward vs. PPO's explicit reward
Diagnosing PPO instability via the DPO framework
Consistency under preference data distributions

outline.description: A look at how DPO performs in the real world. This chapter covers the experimental setup, various tasks, and the results compared to PPO and other baselines.
subtopics: Experimental setup: Sentiment generation, summarization, and dialogue tasks
Evaluating the Reward-KL Frontier: Efficiency of DPO vs. PPO
Performance on real-world datasets (Reddit TL;DR and Anthropic HH)
Generalization: Performance on out-of-distribution data (CNN/DailyMail)
GPT-4 as a proxy for human judgment: Reliability and validation
Complexity analysis: DPO as a lightweight alternative to Best-of-N sampling

outline.description: The final chapter summarizes the impact of DPO on the field of AI alignment and discusses the limitations and future research paths.
subtopics: Summary of DPO's advantages: Stability, simplicity, and performance
Reducing the barrier to entry for preference learning
Limitations: Reward over-optimization and distribution shift
Future work: Scaling to larger models and other modalities
Final thoughts on the future of efficient alignment
